sources.quote: Habeas lawsuits increased by over 85 times during the past year, while naturalization suits were 1.8 times higher than in March 2025.
sources.searcher_note: Court-record count: 9,059 habeas suits in Mar 2026 (ours about 8,820), 105 in Mar 2025, 31,357 Oct 2025-Mar 2026; the 9,059 figure sits in Table 1, not prose. No share of all civil cases, no outcomes

sources.outlet: Joe.My.God. (blog excerpt of Politico, Kyle Cheney, 2026-05-13)
sources.quote: More than 10,000 times, judges have said those detentions, typically carried out with no opportunity for detainees to plead their case, were illegal. That's roughly 90 percent of all cases
sources.searcher_note: Excerpt of Politico's ruling tracker: detainees win about 9 in 10. Politico original (politico.com/news/2026/05/13/10k-rulings-ice-mandatory-detention-trump-analysis-00914195) could not be fetched or searched: domain blocked to this tool

sources.outlet: Working Immigrants (repost of Politico, Kyle Cheney)
sources.quote: The 15,000 rulings against the administration compare to about 2,200 instances in which judges upheld ICE detentions.
sources.searcher_note: Post-cutoff. Politico's one-year tally: about 87% for detainees; our closed-case split is 7,340 vs 831 (about 90%), different unit (rulings vs closed cases) and window

sources.quote: Immigrants filed more habeas cases in the first 13 months of the second Trump administration than in the past three administrations combined, including his first.
sources.searcher_note: Live tracker, published Feb 2026, data updated to 2026-09-22 (post-cutoff): 81,155 habeas cases since Jan 2025; says new cases slowed from April 2026. No civil-docket share

sources.quote: The federal courts are dealing with a barrage of immigration-related lawsuits, with more filed over the past year than any period in history.
sources.searcher_note: Body behind subscriber wall; only the opening line was visible

notes: The surge itself (monthly habeas counts, Mar 2026 near 9,000) and detainee win rates near 90% are widely reported. Not found in any source: the 24%-of-all-new-federal-civil-cases share, the Oct 2024 count of 33, and the 7,340 vs 831 closed-case split. TRAC's Mar 2026 count (9,059) is within 3% of ours. Politico's original tracker could not be opened (domain blocked). Query 5 auto-expanded into five internal searches, so stopped at five logged queries.
